summary: An early 1969 memo on functional specifications for the ARPA Network. It belongs to the first wave of notes in which the Network Working Group worked out what the network should do and how connected computers would use it. It is a planning document rather than a finished specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC is titled ARPA Network Functional Specifications and is dated 5 May 1969. The available text extraction leaves most of its handwritten pages unreadable, so the specific functions it proposed cannot be explained from that text.

sections.title: Document Identification
sections.content:
The first page identifies the title as ARPA Network Functional Specifications, names G. Deloche as author, gives the University of California at Los Angeles as the installation, and dates the document 5 May 1969.

The remaining extracted pages consist mainly of images and unclear handwriting. The readable text does not provide a reliable account of the specification's contents.
sections.plainLanguage: The document's title page identifies it as a set of ARPA Network functional specifications from 5 May 1969. The readable extraction does not make the detailed proposals clear.

sections.title: Limits of the Available Text
sections.content:
The source available for this explainer contains scanned page images with fragments of handwritten text. Those fragments do not support a dependable description of particular network functions, formats or procedures.

This account therefore reports only the identifying details that can be read in the source, rather than guessing at the meaning of unclear diagrams or notes.
sections.plainLanguage: The surviving text is too unclear to explain the technical details accurately. Only the document identity and date can be stated with confidence.

sections.title: Record and Status
sections.content:
The unit metadata records the RFC's status as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The readable source itself identifies this as a Network Working Group request for comment numbered 8.

The available material supports describing this document as a dated specification document, but not asserting what later work adopted its proposals.
sections.plainLanguage: The metadata gives this RFC an Unknown status and lists no replacement or update. The readable material does not show what later documents may have done with its proposals.
